title: Pie Face
description:
Over the summer of 2017 I took my turn suffering at Fuel (as most Ottawa devs did in the 2010s). I basically joined as they were starting to build a mobile version of the children's board game Pie Face, took over the project, completed it, then left the company!

![](/assets/projects/career/pie-face/screenshot-1.webp)![](/assets/projects/career/pie-face/screenshot-3.webp)

Players would challenge friends to a brief minigame, after which the winner got to throw a pie at the loser. The pies came in a wide variety of "flavors" and were applied to the target's profile picture as a visual effect.

![](/assets/projects/career/pie-face/screenshot-4.webp)![](/assets/projects/career/pie-face/screenshot-5.webp)

The game itself was frankly absurd, and failed to become a runaway success, but it was plenty of fun to build. I worked with artists to set up a pipeline for defining new pie types, and to build the system for applying pie effects to the user's picture (you can't tell from these screenshots, but the victim's face would pop out like a 3D model and animate, on top of the special effects added to them).
